/**
 * Balance period and the two rate adjustments, per docs/research/01-balance-period-and-regulator.md.
 *
 *   T = 2π √(I / k)          k ∝ 1 / L_active
 *   rate (s/day) ≈ −43200 · ΔL/L  ≈ −43200 · ΔI/I   (first order; exact forms below)
 */
export interface BalanceSpec {
  /** Moment of inertia, kg·m². */
  inertia: number;
  /** Hairspring torsional stiffness at the reference active length, N·m/rad. */
  stiffness: number;
  /** Reference active length of the hairspring, m. */
  activeLength: number;
  /** Outer coil radius where the regulator pins ride, m. Sets length change per degree of index. */
  regulatorRadius: number;
}

export interface RateAdjustments {
  /** Regulator index angle, degrees. Positive = toward Fast (shortens the active length). */
  regulatorIndex: number;
  /** Fractional change of inertia from timing screws / weights. Positive = more inertia = slower. */
  inertiaTrim: number;
}

export const SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86400;

/** Active length after the regulator moves the pins by `indexDeg` toward Fast. */
export function activeLength(b: BalanceSpec, indexDeg: number): number {
  return b.activeLength - (b.regulatorRadius * indexDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
}

/** Stiffness at a given active length (k ∝ 1/L). */
export function stiffnessAt(b: BalanceSpec, length: number): number {
  return (b.stiffness * b.activeLength) / length;
}

/** Natural period in seconds for the given adjustments. */
export function period(b: BalanceSpec, a: RateAdjustments): number {
  const I = b.inertia * (1 + a.inertiaTrim);
  const k = stiffnessAt(b, activeLength(b, a.regulatorIndex));
  return 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(I / k);
}

/** Nominal period from the calibre's beat rate (beats per hour; one beat is a half period). */
export const nominalPeriod = (beatRate: number) => 7200 / beatRate;

/** Rate in seconds per day from an actual period against the nominal one. Positive = fast. */
export function rateSecondsPerDay(actualPeriod: number, nominal: number): number {
  return SECONDS_PER_DAY * (nominal / actualPeriod - 1);
}

/** A balance spec whose natural period at zero adjustment equals the beat rate exactly. */
export function balanceForBeatRate(beatRate: number, inertia: number, activeLengthM: number, regulatorRadiusM: number): BalanceSpec {
  const T = nominalPeriod(beatRate);
  const stiffness = inertia * (2 * Math.PI / T) ** 2;
  return { inertia, stiffness, activeLength: activeLengthM, regulatorRadius: regulatorRadiusM };
}
EOF

    expect(rateSecondsPerDay(period(modern, { ...zero, inertiaTrim: 0.0035 }), nominal)).toBeCloseTo(-150, -1);
  });
});

## Numbers and formulas to use in the simulation

| Item | Recommendation | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Beat definition | 1 beat = 1 half-swing = 1 tick; beat period = 3600/bph; T = 7200/bph | High (verified) |
| Default calibre beat rate | 28,800 bph (4 Hz), optional second calibre 18,000 bph (2.5 Hz) | High |
| Rate | `rate_s_per_day = (T_nominal / T_measured - 1) * 86400`, average over many beats; + = fast | High (tg source) |
| Beat error | Display `abs(d2 - d1) / 2` in ms (equals the trace-line separation, matches tg); note in GLOSSARY that some machines may show the full difference | Medium (tg verified; Witschi convention unverified) |
| Amplitude | `A = (lift / 2) / sin(pi * dt / T)` where dt = unlock-to-lock time; invert to produce dt from the simulated amplitude | High (tg source, SHM derivation) |
| Lift angle | Parameter per calibre; machine default 52°, sim calibre 50° for an ETA 2824-2-like movement, 44° for a 6497-like pocket calibre | High for 52° default and ETA 50°; Medium for others |
| Healthy amplitude | 270° to 300° dial up at full wind; below 200° is a fault; trace invalid below 135° | Medium (secondary only) |
| Healthy rate / beat error | Within ±10 s/d and under 0.5 ms as "healthy"; ±12 s/d ETA Standard; puzzle "runs fast" at +40 s/d is clearly out of spec | Medium |
| Trace geometry | One dot per beat, x = tick offset mod beat period, slope ∝ rate, two lines separated by beat error; show about 300 beats per screen (about 37 s at 28,800 bph) | High for the mechanism; Medium for the screen scale |
| Beat sounds | Three pulses per beat: unlock, impulse, lock; pulse 1 to pulse 3 spans the lift angle (7 to 12 ms at 280°) | Medium (Witschi description is second-hand) |

Sources: `tg` source files `algo.c`, `computer.c`, `output_panel.c`, `tg.h` at https://github.com/vacaboja/tg ; Witschi Watch Expert III leaflet (cousinsuk.com/PDF/skus/643_leaflet_watchexpertIII t20214.pdf), Chronoscope X1 leaflet (cousinsuk.com/PDF/skus/3531_T32439_leaflet_chronoscope-X1 (G2).pdf), WisioScope page https://www.witschi.com/en/?p=2757 ; ETA CT 2824-2 https://shopb2b.eta.ch/technicaldocuments/index/pdf/id/1883 and /1884 ; https://ciechanow.ski/mechanical-watch/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ETA_SA ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lever_escapement ; https://calibercorner.com/lift-angle/ ; https://calibercorner.com/amplitude/ ; https://watchguy.co.uk/cgi-bin/lift_angles ; https://watchguy.co.uk/?p=2502 ; https://www.watchrepairtalk.com/topic/2727-how-does-the-timegrapheror-vibrograph-measure-amplitude/ ; Weishi 1000 manual (manuals.online, via search snippet only).

/**
 * Tick times of a sinusoidal balance, θ(t) = A·sin(ωt), that engages the fork whenever it
 * crosses the notch centre. If the hairspring's rest position is offset from the notch centre
 * by `beatOffset`, the crossings are unevenly spaced: that is beat error, and it grows as
 * amplitude falls (the same offset is a larger fraction of a smaller swing).
 *
 * Each tick also carries the unlock-to-lock time the timegrapher hears: the time the balance
 * spends inside the lift angle, which is what encodes amplitude in the sound.
 * See docs/research/02-beat-rates-and-timegrapher.md.
 */
export interface Tick {
  /** Absolute time of the tick (balance passing the notch centre), seconds. */
  t: number;
  /** Time from the unlock pulse to the lock pulse within this beat, seconds. */
  liftDuration: number;
  /** Alternates each beat. */
  parity: 0 | 1;
}

export interface TickSource {
  /** Actual period of the balance, seconds. */
  period: number;
  /** Amplitude, degrees. */
  amplitude: number;
  /** Notch centre's angle from the hairspring rest position, degrees. Zero = in beat. */
  beatOffset: number;
  /** Balance travel while engaged with the fork, degrees. */
  liftAngle: number;
}

/** Time the balance spends crossing an angular band of `band` degrees centred on `centre`. */
function crossingDuration(s: TickSource, centre: number, band: number): number {
  const omega = (2 * Math.PI) / s.period;
  const A = s.amplitude;
  const lo = Math.max(-A, Math.min(A, centre - band / 2));
  const hi = Math.max(-A, Math.min(A, centre + band / 2));
  return Math.abs(Math.asin(hi / A) - Math.asin(lo / A)) / omega;
}

/** The two half-period intervals between successive crossings of the notch centre. */
export function beatIntervals(s: TickSource): [number, number] {
  if (Math.abs(s.beatOffset) >= s.amplitude) return [s.period, 0]; // never crosses: stopped
  const omega = (2 * Math.PI) / s.period;
  const phi = Math.asin(s.beatOffset / s.amplitude);
  const d1 = (Math.PI - 2 * phi) / omega;
  return [d1, s.period - d1];
}

/** `count` consecutive ticks starting at time `start` (which is itself a tick of parity 0). */
export function tickTimes(s: TickSource, start: number, count: number): Tick[] {
  const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals(s);
  const lift = crossingDuration(s, s.beatOffset, s.liftAngle);
  const out: Tick[] = [];
  let t = start;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    out.push({ t, liftDuration: lift, parity: (i % 2) as 0 | 1 });
    t += i % 2 === 0 ? d1 : d2;
  }
  return out;
}
EOF
cat > src/core/timegrapher/analyze.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * The instrument. Reads a window of ticks and reports what a bench timegrapher reports.
 * Formulas per docs/research/02-beat-rates-and-timegrapher.md (verified against the `tg`
 * open-source timegrapher):
 *   rate  = (T_nominal / T_measured − 1) · 86400          (+ = fast)
 *   beat error = |d2 − d1| / 2                             (equals trace-line separation)
 *   amplitude = (lift / 2) / sin(π · dt / T)               (dt = unlock-to-lock time)
 */
import type { Tick } from "../oscillator/ticks";

export interface Reading {
  rateSecondsPerDay: number;
  beatErrorMs: number;
  amplitudeDeg: number;
  /** One point per tick: beat index and the tick's offset from the nominal grid, ms. */
  trace: { beat: number; offsetMs: number; parity: 0 | 1 }[];
  beats: number;
}

export function analyze(ticks: Tick[], nominalPeriod: number, liftAngleDeg: number): Reading | null {
  if (ticks.length < 4) return null;
  const beat = nominalPeriod / 2;
  const n = ticks.length;
  // Measured period from first and last tick of matching parity (whole periods between them).
  const lastSame = n - 1 - ((n - 1) % 2);
  const periods = lastSame / 2;
  const measuredPeriod = (ticks[lastSame].t - ticks[0].t) / periods;
  const rateSecondsPerDay = (nominalPeriod / measuredPeriod - 1) * 86400;

  let d1 = 0, d2 = 0, c1 = 0, c2 = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < n; i++) {
    const d = ticks[i].t - ticks[i - 1].t;
    if (ticks[i - 1].parity === 0) { d1 += d; c1++; } else { d2 += d; c2++; }
  }
  const beatErrorMs = c1 && c2 ? (Math.abs(d2 / c2 - d1 / c1) / 2) * 1000 : 0;

  const dt = ticks.reduce((a, k) => a + k.liftDuration, 0) / n;
  const amplitudeDeg = liftAngleDeg / 2 / Math.sin((Math.PI * dt) / measuredPeriod);

  const trace = ticks.map((k, i) => ({ beat: i, offsetMs: (k.t - ticks[0].t - i * beat) * 1000, parity: k.parity }));
  return { rateSecondsPerDay, beatErrorMs, amplitudeDeg, trace, beats: n };
}
EOF

import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { tickTimes, beatIntervals } from "../../src/core/oscillator/ticks";
import { analyze } from "../../src/core/timegrapher/analyze";

const T = 0.4; // 18,000 bph

describe("ticks", () => {
  it("are evenly spaced when in beat and sum to the period", () => {
    const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals({ period: T, amplitude: 270, beatOffset: 0, liftAngle: 52 });
    expect(d1).toBeCloseTo(T / 2, 12);
    expect(d1 + d2).toBeCloseTo(T, 12);
  });
  it("become uneven with a beat offset, more so at lower amplitude", () => {
    const err = (A: number) => { const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals({ period: T, amplitude: A, beatOffset: 5, liftAngle: 52 }); return Math.abs(d2 - d1) / 2; };
    expect(err(270)).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(err(180)).toBeGreaterThan(err(270));
  });
});

describe("timegrapher reading (docs/research/02-beat-rates-and-timegrapher.md)", () => {
  const read = (period: number, amplitude: number, beatOffset: number, lift = 52) =>
    analyze(tickTimes({ period, amplitude, beatOffset, liftAngle: lift }, 0, 300), T, lift)!;

  it("reads zero rate, zero beat error and the true amplitude for a perfect watch", () => {
    const r = read(T, 270, 0);
    expect(r.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeCloseTo(0, 6);
    expect(r.beatErrorMs).toBeCloseTo(0, 9);
    expect(r.amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(270, 6);
  });

  it("reads +40 s/day when the period is short by the matching fraction", () => {
    const r = read(T / (1 + 40 / 86400), 270, 0);
    expect(r.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeCloseTo(40, 6);
  });

  it("reports beat error in ms matching the interval asymmetry", () => {
    const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals({ period: T, amplitude: 270, beatOffset: 4, liftAngle: 52 });
    const r = read(T, 270, 4);
    expect(r.beatErrorMs).toBeCloseTo((Math.abs(d2 - d1) / 2) * 1000, 9);
    expect(r.beatErrorMs).toBeGreaterThan(0.5); // clearly "out of beat" by the healthy threshold
  });

  it("amplitude round-trips through the lift-angle formula at any amplitude", () => {
    for (const A of [150, 200, 250, 300]) expect(read(T, A, 0).amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(A, 6);
  });

  it("misreads amplitude if the wrong lift angle is assumed (52° set, 50° true)", () => {
    const ticks = tickTimes({ period: T, amplitude: 250, beatOffset: 0, liftAngle: 50 }, 0, 100);
    const r = analyze(ticks, T, 52)!;
    expect(r.amplitudeDeg).toBeGreaterThan(255); // reads high, as calibercorner's worked example shows
  });

  it("draws a trace whose slope is the rate and whose two lines are separated by the beat error", () => {
    const r = read(T / (1 + 40 / 86400), 270, 4);
    const even = r.trace.filter((p) => p.parity === 0), odd = r.trace.filter((p) => p.parity === 1);
    const slope = (even[even.length - 1].offsetMs - even[0].offsetMs) / (even[even.length - 1].beat - even[0].beat); // ms per beat
    expect(slope).toBeLessThan(0); // ticks arrive early when fast
    expect(Math.abs(slope) * (86400 / (T / 2)) / 1000).toBeCloseTo(40, 0); // ms/beat → s/day
    const sep = Math.abs(odd[10].offsetMs - (even[10].offsetMs + even[11].offsetMs) / 2);
    expect(sep).toBeCloseTo(r.beatErrorMs, 6);
  });
});

[V] Airy (1826) / Hoyng (2015) averaged (KBM) equations, per oscillation: dλ/dt = −ελ + ∮ m cosψ dψ (amplitude); rate − 1 = −(1/λ)∮ m sinψ dψ (escapement error; the −λ²/16 circular-error term is a pendulum term and is absent for a Hooke's-law hairspring). Sign rule: impulse before the zero crossing → gain, after → loss; magnitude ∝ (impulse energy / oscillator energy) × tan(impulse phase). Single impulse of energy e at angle φ₁: Δrate = −(e/2πλ²)·φ₁/√(λ²−φ₁²). Everything below is this model plus an empirical hairspring term.

## Numbers and model to use in the simulation

| Quantity | Recommendation | Confidence / source |
|---|---|---|
| Mainspring torque T(t), t in hours, healthy manual calibre | T/T₀ = 1 − 0.15·(t/24) for 0 ≤ t ≤ 36 h (linear, −15 % in 24 h); then fall linearly to 0 at t ≈ 42 h ("ineffective turns"); stop when amplitude < ~120° | Medium: WatchTime 15 %/day rule; ~6 turns × 7.5 h/turn; Britten via vintagewatchstraps |
| Amplitude from torque | A = A₀·(T/T₀)^k, k = 0.7 (between viscous k=0.5 and Coulomb k=1); A₀ = 280° dial-up, 260° vertical | Medium for the law (Hoyng Eq. 19, App. C); low for k |
| Amplitude curve, healthy watch | 0 h 280°, 12 h 265°, 24 h 250°, 36 h 235°, 40 h ~190°, stops ≈ 42 h | Medium: Witschi 270–310° full wind; bench 10–15 % drop at 24 h |
| Amplitude curve, "afternoon slump" puzzle (tired/thin spring or dirty train) | use T/T₀ = 1 − 0.40·(t/24): 280° → ~200° at 24 h | Medium: brief's figure matches BHI "minimum 200° at 24 h" and WRT ">225° healthy" |
| Escapement error (always a loss, grows at low amplitude) | r_esc(A) = −k_e·(A_ref/A − 1), A_ref = 280°, k_e ≈ 8 s/d (gives −1.1 s/d at 250°, −3.7 at 200°, −6.9 at 150°) | Sign: high (Airy, Hoyng, patent, SJX). Magnitude: low–medium (patent's 2–8 s/d over 300°→150°) |
| Hairspring/regulator-pin term (a gain at low amplitude, tunable by pin gap and centring) | r_pin(A) = +k_p·(A_ref − A)/10°, k_p default 0.8 s/d per 10° (net ≈ +1 s/d per 10° between 280° and 250°, matching Witschi example); k_p → 0 with a wide gap or overcoil + no pins; k_p ≈ 5–8 when the spring rests on a pin (fault state) | Medium for sign and that it dominates in flat-spring watches; low for the number |
| Net rate vs amplitude | r(A) = r₀ + r_esc(A) + r_pin(A); net sign is positive (gains as amplitude falls) for the default flat-spring calibre, negative for an overcoil calibre with k_p = 0 | Medium |
| Knocking threshold | if A > 330° (dial-up) clip the swing at 330° and add a gain of order +50 to +300 s/d with a noisy trace; show amplitude as unreliable | Medium for threshold (320–330° quoted widely, Horopedia 280–300° for older geometry); low for the gain figure |
| Lift angle for timegrapher amplitude | 51° (Witschi "approximately 51°"), 52° also common; lever engaged ≈ ±15° of swing (Stoimenov) | High |
| Amplitude reading formula | A = λ / (2·sin(π·f·t_lift)), f in Hz, t_lift in s | High (Witschi Eq. 6) |

/**
 * Mainspring torque over the wind, and the amplitude it produces, per
 * docs/research/03-amplitude-and-isochronism.md.
 *
 *   torque fraction  τ(t) = 1 − fall·(t/24)  for t ≤ 36 h, then linear to 0 at 42 h
 *   amplitude        A = A_pos · τ^k,  k = 0.7
 */
export interface MainspringSpec {
  /** Fractional torque lost per 24 h of running: 0.15 healthy, 0.40 for a tired spring. */
  fallPerDay: number;
  /** Hours of roughly linear torque before the "ineffective turns". */
  linearHours: number;
  /** Hours at which torque reaches zero. */
  stopHours: number;
}

export const HEALTHY_MAINSPRING: MainspringSpec = { fallPerDay: 0.15, linearHours: 36, stopHours: 42 };
export const TIRED_MAINSPRING: MainspringSpec = { ...HEALTHY_MAINSPRING, fallPerDay: 0.4 };

export function torqueFraction(m: MainspringSpec, hoursSinceWind: number): number {
  const t = Math.max(0, hoursSinceWind);
  const atLinearEnd = 1 - m.fallPerDay * (m.linearHours / 24);
  if (t <= m.linearHours) return Math.max(0, 1 - m.fallPerDay * (t / 24));
  if (t >= m.stopHours) return 0;
  return atLinearEnd * (1 - (t - m.linearHours) / (m.stopHours - m.linearHours));
}

/** Exponent relating amplitude to torque: 0.5 for viscous losses, 1 for Coulomb; 0.7 recommended. */
export const AMPLITUDE_EXPONENT = 0.7;

/** Amplitude below which the sim treats the watch as stopped. */
export const STOP_AMPLITUDE_DEG = 120;

/** Amplitude above which the impulse pin strikes the fork's back: "knocking" / rebanking. */
export const KNOCK_AMPLITUDE_DEG = 330;

export function amplitudeFromTorque(fullTorqueAmplitudeDeg: number, torque: number): number {
  return fullTorqueAmplitudeDeg * Math.pow(Math.max(0, torque), AMPLITUDE_EXPONENT);
}

/**
 * Rate corrections that depend on amplitude, s/day. Both are referenced to A_ref so a healthy
 * watch at full wind reads its regulated rate.
 *   escapement error  r_esc = −k_e · (A_ref/A − 1)       always a loss, grows at low amplitude
 *   regulator pins    r_pin = +k_p · (A_ref − A)/10°     a gain at low amplitude in flat-spring watches
 */
export interface IsochronismSpec {
  refAmplitudeDeg: number;
  /** s/day scale of the escapement error; ~8 recommended. */
  escapementCoefficient: number;
  /** s/day per 10° of amplitude from the regulator-pin effect; 0.8 default, ~5–8 when the spring rests on a pin. */
  pinCoefficient: number;
}

export const DEFAULT_ISOCHRONISM: IsochronismSpec = { refAmplitudeDeg: 280, escapementCoefficient: 8, pinCoefficient: 0.8 };

export function escapementErrorSecondsPerDay(s: IsochronismSpec, amplitudeDeg: number): number {
  if (amplitudeDeg <= 0) return 0;
  return -s.escapementCoefficient * (s.refAmplitudeDeg / amplitudeDeg - 1);
}

export function pinErrorSecondsPerDay(s: IsochronismSpec, amplitudeDeg: number): number {
  return s.pinCoefficient * ((s.refAmplitudeDeg - amplitudeDeg) / 10);
}
EOF
cat > src/core/watch.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * The whole watch as one pure reading: given a calibre, its faults, the user's adjustments and
 * the hours since winding, what is the balance doing right now? Everything the views and the
 * timegrapher need derives from this; nothing here draws or accumulates.
 */
import { type BalanceSpec, type RateAdjustments, period as balancePeriod, nominalPeriod, rateSecondsPerDay } from "./oscillator/period";
import { type MainspringSpec, type IsochronismSpec, torqueFraction, amplitudeFromTorque, escapementErrorSecondsPerDay, pinErrorSecondsPerDay, STOP_AMPLITUDE_DEG, KNOCK_AMPLITUDE_DEG } from "./oscillator/amplitude";
import { poiseRateSecondsPerDay } from "./oscillator/poise";

export type Position = "DU" | "DD" | "CU" | "CR" | "CD" | "CL";

export const POSITIONS: { id: Position; label: string; tilt: number; /** balance angle that points straight down at rest */ down: number }[] = [
  { id: "DU", label: "dial up", tilt: 0, down: 0 },
  { id: "DD", label: "dial down", tilt: 0, down: 0 },
  { id: "CU", label: "crown up", tilt: Math.PI / 2, down: 0 },
  { id: "CR", label: "crown right", tilt: Math.PI / 2, down: 90 },
  { id: "CD", label: "crown down", tilt: Math.PI / 2, down: 180 },
  { id: "CL", label: "crown left", tilt: Math.PI / 2, down: 270 },
];

export interface WatchSpec {
  beatRate: number;
  liftAngle: number;
  balance: BalanceSpec;
  mainspring: MainspringSpec;
  isochronism: IsochronismSpec;
  /** Amplitude dial up at full torque, and how much less in any vertical position. */
  fullWindAmplitudeDeg: number;
  verticalDropDeg: number;
}

/** Hidden faults a puzzle bakes into the watch, plus the user's adjustments on top. */
export interface WatchSettings extends RateAdjustments {
  /** Notch centre's angle from the hairspring rest, degrees. Zero = in beat. */
  beatOffsetDeg: number;
  /** Balance unbalance, kg·m, and where the heavy spot sits on the rim, degrees. */
  unbalance: number;
  heavySpotDeg: number;
  position: Position;
  hoursSinceWind: number;
}

export interface WatchReading {
  running: boolean;
  knocking: boolean;
  amplitudeDeg: number;
  torqueFraction: number;
  /** True period of the balance including every error term, seconds. */
  period: number;
  /** Rate the watch actually keeps, s/day, and its decomposition. */
  rateSecondsPerDay: number;
  rateTerms: { regulation: number; escapement: number; pins: number; poise: number; knocking: number };
  beatOffsetDeg: number;
  liftAngle: number;
}

export const ZERO_SETTINGS: WatchSettings = { regulatorIndex: 0, inertiaTrim: 0, beatOffsetDeg: 0, unbalance: 0, heavySpotDeg: 0, position: "DU", hoursSinceWind: 0 };

export function readWatch(w: WatchSpec, s: WatchSettings): WatchReading {
  const pos = POSITIONS.find((p) => p.id === s.position)!;
  const torque = torqueFraction(w.mainspring, s.hoursSinceWind);
  const fullAmp = w.fullWindAmplitudeDeg - (pos.tilt > 0 ? w.verticalDropDeg : 0);
  let amplitude = amplitudeFromTorque(fullAmp, torque);
  const knocking = amplitude > KNOCK_AMPLITUDE_DEG;
  if (knocking) amplitude = KNOCK_AMPLITUDE_DEG;
  const running = amplitude >= STOP_AMPLITUDE_DEG;

  const nominal = nominalPeriod(w.beatRate);
  const regulation = rateSecondsPerDay(balancePeriod(w.balance, s), nominal);
  const escapement = running ? escapementErrorSecondsPerDay(w.isochronism, amplitude) : 0;
  const pins = running ? pinErrorSecondsPerDay(w.isochronism, amplitude) : 0;
  const omega0 = (2 * Math.PI) / nominal;
  const poise = running
    ? poiseRateSecondsPerDay({ unbalance: s.unbalance, heavySpotAngle: ((s.heavySpotDeg - pos.down) * Math.PI) / 180, tilt: pos.tilt, inertia: w.balance.inertia, omega0, amplitude: (amplitude * Math.PI) / 180 })
    : 0;
  const knock = knocking ? 120 : 0;
  const rate = regulation + escapement + pins + poise + knock;
  return {
    running,
    knocking,
    amplitudeDeg: running ? amplitude : 0,
    torqueFraction: torque,
    period: nominal / (1 + rate / 86400),
    rateSecondsPerDay: rate,
    rateTerms: { regulation, escapement, pins, poise, knocking: knock },
    beatOffsetDeg: s.beatOffsetDeg,
    liftAngle: w.liftAngle,
  };
}
EOF

import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { readWatch, ZERO_SETTINGS } from "../../src/core/watch";
import { VINTAGE_18000 } from "../../src/catalog/vintage18000";
import { TIRED_MAINSPRING, torqueFraction, HEALTHY_MAINSPRING } from "../../src/core/oscillator/amplitude";

const w = VINTAGE_18000.watch;

describe("a healthy, regulated watch", () => {
  it("reads ~0 s/day, 280° and runs at full wind dial up", () => {
    const r = readWatch(w, ZERO_SETTINGS);
    expect(r.running).toBe(true);
    expect(r.amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(280, 6);
    expect(Math.abs(r.rateSecondsPerDay)).toBeLessThan(0.01);
    expect(r.period).toBeCloseTo(0.4, 6);
  });

  it("follows the research amplitude curve: ~250° at 24 h, stops by 42 h", () => {
    expect(readWatch(w, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, hoursSinceWind: 24 }).amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(250, -1);
    expect(readWatch(w, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, hoursSinceWind: 42 }).running).toBe(false);
    expect(torqueFraction(HEALTHY_MAINSPRING, 24)).toBeCloseTo(0.85, 9);
  });

  it("gains a little as it runs down (flat-spring default), within a few s/day at 24 h", () => {
    const r24 = readWatch(w, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, hoursSinceWind: 24 });
    expect(r24.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(r24.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeLessThan(5);
    expect(r24.rateTerms.escapement).toBeLessThan(0); // the escapement alone would make it lose
  });
});

describe("puzzle 1: runs fast", () => {
  it("+1.2° of regulator index reads about +40 s/day", () => {
    const r = readWatch(w, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, regulatorIndex: 1.2 });
    expect(r.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeCloseTo(40, -1);
  });
});

describe("puzzle 3: afternoon slump", () => {
  it("a tired mainspring drops to ~200° by 24 h and gains several s/day more than at full wind", () => {
    const tired = { ...w, mainspring: TIRED_MAINSPRING };
    const r0 = readWatch(tired, ZERO_SETTINGS), r24 = readWatch(tired, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, hoursSinceWind: 24 });
    expect(r24.amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(200, -1);
    expect(r24.rateSecondsPerDay - r0.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeGreaterThan(2);
  });
});

describe("puzzle 4: position error", () => {
  it("poise error shows in vertical positions only, with opposite sign crown up vs crown down", () => {
    const s = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, unbalance: 10e-11, heavySpotDeg: 0 };
    const du = readWatch(w, { ...s, position: "DU" as const });
    const cu = readWatch(w, { ...s, position: "CU" as const });
    const cd = readWatch(w, { ...s, position: "CD" as const });
    expect(du.rateTerms.poise).toBe(0);
    expect(cu.rateTerms.poise * cd.rateTerms.poise).toBeLessThan(0);
    expect(cu.amplitudeDeg).toBeCloseTo(250, 6); // 30° vertical drop
  });
});

describe("knocking", () => {
  it("clips amplitude at 330° and adds a large gain", () => {
    const hot = { ...w, fullWindAmplitudeDeg: 350 };
    const r = readWatch(hot, ZERO_SETTINGS);
    expect(r.knocking).toBe(true);
    expect(r.amplitudeDeg).toBe(330);
    expect(r.rateSecondsPerDay).toBeGreaterThan(50);
  });
});

/** Incremental tick stream: extends a window of ticks from the current watch reading. */
import type { Tick } from "../core/oscillator/ticks";
import { beatIntervals } from "../core/oscillator/ticks";
import type { WatchReading } from "../core/watch";

export interface TickWindow { ticks: Tick[]; nextParity: 0 | 1; nextTime: number }

export const emptyWindow = (): TickWindow => ({ ticks: [], nextParity: 0, nextTime: 0 });

/** Append every tick due up to `untilTime` (sim seconds), keeping at most `keep` ticks. */
export function advanceTicks(win: TickWindow, r: WatchReading, untilTime: number, keep: number): TickWindow {
  if (!r.running) return win;
  const src = { period: r.period, amplitude: r.amplitudeDeg, beatOffset: r.beatOffsetDeg, liftAngle: r.liftAngle };
  const [d1, d2] = beatIntervals(src);
  const omega = (2 * Math.PI) / r.period;
  const half = r.liftAngle / 2, A = r.amplitudeDeg, c = r.beatOffsetDeg;
  const clamp = (x: number) => Math.max(-A, Math.min(A, x));
  const lift = Math.abs(Math.asin(clamp(c + half) / A) - Math.asin(clamp(c - half) / A)) / omega;
  const ticks = win.ticks.slice();
  let t = win.nextTime, parity = win.nextParity;
  let guard = 0;
  while (t <= untilTime && guard++ < 100000) {
    ticks.push({ t, liftDuration: lift, parity });
    t += parity === 0 ? d1 : d2;
    parity = parity === 0 ? 1 : 0;
  }
  return { ticks: ticks.length > keep ? ticks.slice(ticks.length - keep) : ticks, nextParity: parity, nextTime: t };
}

/** Timegrapher panel: trace plus readouts. Reads a Reading; computes nothing but pixels. */
import type { Reading } from "../core/timegrapher/analyze";

export interface TimegrapherView {
  reading: Reading | null;
  nominalPeriod: number;
  liftAngle: number;
  running: boolean;
  knocking: boolean;
  /** Sim seconds the trace spans, for the honest label. */
  spanSeconds: number;
}

const fmt = (x: number, d: number) => (x >= 0 ? "+" : "−") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(d);

export function renderTimegrapher(v: TimegrapherView): string {
  const W = 420, H = 300, pad = 36;
  const beatMs = (v.nominalPeriod / 2) * 1000;
  const yRange = beatMs / 2; // ±half a beat period wraps the trace like a real machine
  const r = v.reading;
  const dots = r
    ? r.trace.map((p) => {
        const x = pad + ((W - 2 * pad) * p.beat) / Math.max(1, r.trace.length - 1);
        let off = ((p.offsetMs + yRange) % (2 * yRange) + 2 * yRange) % (2 * yRange) - yRange; // wrap
        const y = H / 2 - (off / yRange) * (H / 2 - pad);
        return `<circle class="dot p${p.parity}" cx="${x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${y.toFixed(1)}" r="1.4"/>`;
      }).join("")
    : "";
  const rate = r && v.running ? fmt(r.rateSecondsPerDay, 0) : "—";
  const amp = r && v.running ? r.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0) : "—";
  const be = r && v.running ? r.beatErrorMs.toFixed(1) : "—";
  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H + 90}" class="timegrapher" data-rate="${r?.rateSecondsPerDay ?? ""}">
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" class="screen"/>
  <line x1="${pad}" y1="${H / 2}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${H / 2}" class="axis"/>
  <text x="${pad}" y="${pad - 10}" class="axislabel">+${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
  <text x="${pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel">−${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
  <text x="${W - pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel" text-anchor="end">${v.spanSeconds.toFixed(0)} s of ticks</text>
  ${v.knocking ? `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">KNOCKING — amplitude unreliable</text>` : ""}
  ${v.running ? dots : `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">no signal — watch stopped</text>`}
  <g class="readouts" transform="translate(0,${H + 8})">
    <text x="${pad}" y="28" class="big">${rate}<tspan class="unit"> s/day</tspan></text>
    <text x="${W / 2}" y="28" class="big" text-anchor="middle">${amp}<tspan class="unit">°</tspan></text>
    <text x="${W - pad}" y="28" class="big" text-anchor="end">${be}<tspan class="unit"> ms</tspan></text>
    <text x="${pad}" y="48" class="small">rate</text>
    <text x="${W / 2}" y="48" class="small" text-anchor="middle">amplitude · lift angle ${v.liftAngle}°</text>
    <text x="${W - pad}" y="48" class="small" text-anchor="end">beat error</text>
  </g>
</svg>`;
}

/** Diagnosis puzzles: a bundled faulty watch, a symptom, a hidden cause, a completion rule. */
import type { WatchSettings, WatchSpec, WatchReading } from "../core/watch";
import { TIRED_MAINSPRING } from "../core/oscillator/amplitude";

export interface Puzzle {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  symptom: string;
  goal: string;
  /** Hidden faults added to the user's settings. */
  faults: Partial<WatchSettings>;
  /** Hidden changes to the calibre itself. */
  specOverride?: (w: WatchSpec) => WatchSpec;
  /** Band the reading must stay inside, and for how long (sim seconds). */
  band: (r: WatchReading) => boolean;
  holdSeconds: number;
  explanation: string;
  /** Which controls this puzzle shows. */
  controls: ("regulator" | "beat" | "wind" | "screws" | "position")[];
}

export const PUZZLES: Puzzle[] = [
  {
    id: "runs-fast",
    title: "Runs fast",
    symptom: "The owner says it gains about 40 seconds a day.",
    goal: "Bring the rate within ±5 s/day and hold it there for 60 seconds of ticks.",
    faults: { regulatorIndex: 1.2 },
    band: (r) => r.running && Math.abs(r.rateSecondsPerDay) <= 5,
    holdSeconds: 60,
    explanation:
      "The regulator index was sitting toward Fast. Its pins shorten the hairspring's active length, which stiffens it and shortens the period: the balance swings a little quicker every beat, and 86,400 seconds of quicker beats add up to 40 s/day. Moving the index toward Slow lengthens the spring and brings the period back.",
    controls: ["regulator"],
  },
  {
    id: "out-of-beat",
    title: "Out of beat",
    symptom: "The tick sounds uneven: tick-tock, tick-tock, like a limp. The rate is fine.",
    goal: "Bring the beat error under 0.5 ms and hold it for 60 seconds of ticks.",
    faults: { beatOffsetDeg: 6 },
    band: (r) => r.running,
    holdSeconds: 60,
    explanation:
      "The hairspring's rest position was rotated away from the fork's centre line, so the balance passed the notch late on one side and early on the other. The two half-swings had different lengths. Rotating the stud carrier (the beat adjustment) turns the rest position back under the fork.",
    controls: ["beat"],
  },
  {
    id: "afternoon-slump",
    title: "Afternoon slump",
    symptom: "Fine in the morning, drifts by evening. Regulating it only moves the problem.",
    goal: "Drag the state of wind through the day and explain what you see. There is no knob that fixes this.",
    faults: {},
    specOverride: (w) => ({ ...w, mainspring: TIRED_MAINSPRING }),
    band: () => false,
    holdSeconds: Infinity,
    explanation:
      "The mainspring is tired: its torque falls 40 % over a day instead of 15 %. Amplitude follows torque, and rate follows amplitude: in a flat-spring watch the regulator pins make it gain as the swing shrinks, while the escapement alone would make it lose. Some errors are physics, not adjustment. The fix is a new mainspring, not the regulator.",
    controls: ["wind", "regulator"],
  },
  {
    id: "position-error",
    title: "Position error",
    symptom: "Keeps good time on the nightstand, loses on the wrist.",
    goal: "Compare positions on the trace and find where the heavy spot is. Bring the spread between dial up and crown down under 10 s/day.",
    faults: { unbalance: 10e-11, heavySpotDeg: 0 },
    band: (r) => r.running && Math.abs(r.rateTerms.poise) <= 2,
    holdSeconds: 60,
    explanation:
      "The balance is out of poise: one spot on the rim is heavier. Lying flat, gravity pulls along the axis and nothing happens. Standing up, gravity tugs the heavy spot on every swing, helping or hindering depending on where it sits. Below about 220° of amplitude the error has one sign, above it the other, which is why it changes between morning and evening too.",
    controls: ["position", "screws", "wind"],
  },
];

/** Named states for the verify-render skill. Each sets puzzle, settings and animation phase. */
import type { WatchSettings } from "../core/watch";
import type { Phase } from "../core/escapement/kinematics";

export interface NamedState {
  describe: string;
  puzzle: string | null;
  settings: Partial<WatchSettings>;
  /** Freeze the animation at the middle of this escapement phase on this beat (0 entry, 1 exit). */
  freeze?: { phase: Phase; beat: 0 | 1; frac?: number };
  /** Simulated seconds of ticks to accumulate before the shot. */
  simSeconds: number;
  expect: { phase?: Phase; rateWithin?: [number, number]; amplitudeWithin?: [number, number]; beatErrorBelow?: number; running?: boolean };
}

export const STATES: Record<string, NamedState> = {
  "healthy-full-wind": { describe: "Free play, no puzzle: healthy watch, dial up, full wind. Trace flat, two lines overlapping, ~280°.", puzzle: null, settings: {}, simSeconds: 120, expect: { rateWithin: [-1, 1], amplitudeWithin: [275, 285], beatErrorBelow: 0.1, running: true } },
  "runs-fast-start": { describe: "Puzzle 1 as loaded: trace sloping (ticks early), readout about +40 s/day.", puzzle: "runs-fast", settings: {}, simSeconds: 120, expect: { rateWithin: [35, 45], running: true } },
  "runs-fast-fixed": { describe: "Puzzle 1 with the regulator moved 1.2° toward Slow: trace flat, rate near 0.", puzzle: "runs-fast", settings: { regulatorIndex: -1.2 }, simSeconds: 120, expect: { rateWithin: [-3, 3], running: true } },
  "out-of-beat": { describe: "Puzzle 2 as loaded: two trace lines clearly separated, beat error well above 0.5 ms.", puzzle: "out-of-beat", settings: {}, simSeconds: 120, expect: { running: true } },
  "slump-evening": { describe: "Puzzle 3 at 24 h of wind: amplitude near 200°, watch gaining a few s/day.", puzzle: "afternoon-slump", settings: { hoursSinceWind: 24 }, simSeconds: 120, expect: { amplitudeWithin: [190, 210], rateWithin: [2, 15], running: true } },
  "stopped": { describe: "Healthy watch at 42 h: no signal, balance still, readouts blank.", puzzle: null, settings: { hoursSinceWind: 42 }, simSeconds: 60, expect: { running: false } },
  "entry-impulse": { describe: "Movement frozen mid entry impulse: pin in notch, tooth on the entry impulse face.", puzzle: null, settings: {}, freeze: { phase: "impulse", beat: 0 }, simSeconds: 10, expect: { phase: "impulse" } },
  "exit-lock": { describe: "Movement frozen at exit lock: pin far from notch, tooth resting on the exit locking face.", puzzle: null, settings: {}, freeze: { phase: "lock", beat: 1 }, simSeconds: 10, expect: { phase: "lock" } },
};

cat > src/main.ts <<'EOF'
import { VINTAGE_18000 } from "./catalog/vintage18000";
import { readWatch, ZERO_SETTINGS, POSITIONS, type WatchSettings, type WatchReading, type WatchSpec } from "./core/watch";
import { nominalPeriod } from "./core/oscillator/period";
import { initialPose, step, type EscapementPose, type Phase } from "./core/escapement/kinematics";
import { shapes, stonePenetration } from "./core/escapement/shapes";
import { derived } from "./core/escapement/params";
import { CONTACT_TOL } from "./core/escapement/kinematics";
import { analyze, type Reading } from "./core/timegrapher/analyze";
import { advanceTicks, emptyWindow, type TickWindow } from "./app/ticker";
import { renderMovement } from "./view/movement";
import { renderTimegrapher } from "./view/timegrapher";
import { PUZZLES, type Puzzle } from "./puzzles";
import { STATES } from "./verify/states";

const calibre = VINTAGE_18000;
const esc = calibre.escapement;
const T = nominalPeriod(calibre.beatRate);
const TRACE_BEATS = 300;
/** Timegrapher clock runs this many times faster than the wall clock (decision: two clocks). */
const SIM_SPEEDUP = 60;

// ---------- state ----------
let puzzle: Puzzle | null = PUZZLES[0];
let user: WatchSettings = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS };
let animSpeed = 1;
let animPaused = false;
let animTime = T / 4;
let simTime = 0;
let win: TickWindow = emptyWindow();
let pose: EscapementPose = initialPose(esc, 0);
let reading: WatchReading = readWatch(calibre.watch, user);
let tg: Reading | null = null;
let heldSeconds = 0;
let solved = false;
let lastWall = performance.now();

const spec = (): WatchSpec => (puzzle?.specOverride ? puzzle.specOverride(calibre.watch) : calibre.watch);
const effective = (): WatchSettings => {
  const f = puzzle?.faults ?? {};
  return {
    ...user,
    regulatorIndex: user.regulatorIndex + (f.regulatorIndex ?? 0),
    beatOffsetDeg: user.beatOffsetDeg + (f.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0),
    unbalance: user.unbalance + (f.unbalance ?? 0),
    heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? user.heavySpotDeg,
    inertiaTrim: user.inertiaTrim,
  };
};

// ---------- DOM ----------
const $ = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
const movementEl = $("movement"), tgEl = $("timegrapher"), puzzleEl = $("puzzle");

function balanceAngleAt(t: number) {
  return reading.running ? reading.amplitudeDeg * Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * t) / reading.period) - reading.beatOffsetDeg : -reading.beatOffsetDeg;
}

function recompute() {
  reading = readWatch(spec(), effective());
}

function drawMovement() {
  movementEl.innerHTML = renderMovement(esc, pose, animTime * 1000);
}
function drawTimegrapher() {
  tgEl.innerHTML = renderTimegrapher({ reading: tg, nominalPeriod: T, liftAngle: calibre.liftAngle, running: reading.running, knocking: reading.knocking, spanSeconds: (TRACE_BEATS * T) / 2 });
}
function drawPuzzle() {
  if (!puzzle) { puzzleEl.innerHTML = `<h2>Free play</h2><p>Adjust anything. The timegrapher shows what a watchmaker would see.</p>`; return; }
  const idx = PUZZLES.indexOf(puzzle);
  puzzleEl.innerHTML = `<h2>Puzzle ${idx + 1} · ${puzzle.title}</h2>
    <p class="symptom">${puzzle.symptom}</p>
    <p class="goal"><strong>Goal:</strong> ${puzzle.goal}</p>
    ${Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds) ? `<div class="hold"><div class="bar" style="width:${Math.min(100, (100 * heldSeconds) / puzzle.holdSeconds).toFixed(1)}%"></div><span>${solved ? "solved" : `${heldSeconds.toFixed(0)} / ${puzzle.holdSeconds} s in band`}</span></div>` : ""}
    ${solved || !Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds) ? `<details ${solved ? "open" : ""}><summary>${solved ? "Why it worked" : "Reveal the cause"}</summary><p>${puzzle.explanation}</p></details>` : ""}`;
}
function drawControls() {
  const show = (name: string) => !puzzle || puzzle.controls.includes(name as never) || puzzle.controls.length === 0;
  for (const name of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws", "position"]) $(`ctl-${name}`).hidden = !show(name) && name !== "wind" ? true : !show(name);
  $("readout-rate").textContent = reading.running ? `${reading.rateSecondsPerDay >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(reading.rateSecondsPerDay).toFixed(1)} s/day true rate` : "stopped";
}

// ---------- frame loop ----------
function frame(now: number) {
  const wallDt = Math.min(0.1, (now - lastWall) / 1000);
  lastWall = now;
  if (!animPaused) {
    const dt = wallDt * animSpeed;
    animTime += dt;
    pose = step(esc, pose, balanceAngleAt(animTime), Math.max(dt, 1e-6));
    drawMovement();
  }
  // Timegrapher clock.
  const simDt = wallDt * SIM_SPEEDUP;
  simTime += simDt;
  win = advanceTicks(win, reading, simTime, TRACE_BEATS);
  tg = analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle);
  drawTimegrapher();
  if (puzzle && !solved && Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds)) {
    heldSeconds = puzzle.band(reading) ? heldSeconds + simDt : 0;
    if (heldSeconds >= puzzle.holdSeconds) solved = true;
    drawPuzzle();
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

// ---------- controls ----------
function bindRange(id: string, key: keyof WatchSettings, fmt: (v: number) => string) {
  const el = $<HTMLInputElement>(id), out = $(`${id}-value`);
  const apply = () => { (user as any)[key] = Number(el.value); out.textContent = fmt(Number(el.value)); recompute(); drawControls(); };
  el.oninput = apply; apply();
}
bindRange("regulator", "regulatorIndex", (v) => `${v >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(2)}° ${v > 0 ? "(toward F)" : v < 0 ? "(toward S)" : ""}`);
bindRange("beat", "beatOffsetDeg", (v) => `${v.toFixed(1)}°`);
bindRange("wind", "hoursSinceWind", (v) => `${v.toFixed(0)} h since wound`);
bindRange("screws", "inertiaTrim", (v) => `${(v * 100).toFixed(2)} % inertia`);
$<HTMLSelectElement>("position").onchange = (e) => { user.position = (e.target as HTMLSelectElement).value as WatchSettings["position"]; recompute(); drawControls(); };
$<HTMLSelectElement>("position").innerHTML = POSITIONS.map((p) => `<option value="${p.id}">${p.label}</option>`).join("");
$<HTMLSelectElement>("speed").onchange = (e) => { animSpeed = Number((e.target as HTMLSelectElement).value); };
$("pause").onclick = () => { animPaused = !animPaused; $("pause").textContent = animPaused ? "Play" : "Pause"; };
const puzzleSel = $<HTMLSelectElement>("puzzle-select");
puzzleSel.innerHTML = `<option value="">Free play</option>` + PUZZLES.map((p, i) => `<option value="${p.id}">Puzzle ${i + 1}: ${p.title}</option>`).join("");
function loadPuzzle(id: string | null) {
  puzzle = PUZZLES.find((p) => p.id === id) ?? null;
  puzzleSel.value = puzzle?.id ?? "";
  user = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS };
  for (const id of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws"]) { $<HTMLInputElement>(id).value = "0"; }
  $<HTMLSelectElement>("position").value = "DU";
  heldSeconds = 0; solved = false; win = emptyWindow(); simTime = 0;
  recompute(); drawControls(); drawPuzzle();
  for (const id of ["regulator", "beat", "wind", "screws"]) $<HTMLInputElement>(id).dispatchEvent(new Event("input"));
}
puzzleSel.onchange = () => loadPuzzle(puzzleSel.value || null);
$("calibre-name").textContent = calibre.name;

// ---------- verify-render contract ----------
const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
let named: string | null = null;
function timeForPhase(phase: Phase, beat: 0 | 1, frac: number): number {
  // Scan one period from T/4 with a fresh pose, find the phase window on the requested beat.
  const N = 4000;
  let p = initialPose(esc, balanceAngleAt(T / 4));
  let t = T / 4, start: number | null = null, found: [number, number] | null = null, beatIdx = -1, lastPhase: Phase = p.phase;
  for (let i = 1; i <= N && !found; i++) {
    const nt = T / 4 + (i / N) * T;
    p = step(esc, p, balanceAngleAt(nt), nt - t); t = nt;
    if (p.phase === "unlock" && lastPhase === "lock") beatIdx++;
    if (beatIdx === beat && p.phase === phase && start === null) start = t;
    if (start !== null && p.phase !== phase) found = [start, t];
    lastPhase = p.phase;
  }
  return found ? found[0] + frac * (found[1] - found[0]) : T / 4;
}
if (q.has("state") && STATES[q.get("state")!]) {
  named = q.get("state")!;
  const s = STATES[named];
  loadPuzzle(s.puzzle);
  Object.assign(user, s.settings);
  recompute();
  // Accumulate ticks for the requested sim span, then freeze everything.
  win = advanceTicks(win, reading, s.simSeconds, TRACE_BEATS);
  simTime = s.simSeconds;
  tg = analyze(win.ticks, T, calibre.liftAngle);
  animPaused = true;
  if (s.freeze) {
    animTime = timeForPhase(s.freeze.phase, s.freeze.beat, s.freeze.frac ?? 0.5);
    pose = initialPose(esc, balanceAngleAt(T / 4));
    let t = T / 4;
    while (t < animTime) { const nt = Math.min(animTime, t + 1e-4); pose = step(esc, pose, balanceAngleAt(nt), nt - t); t = nt; }
  }
  drawMovement(); drawTimegrapher(); drawPuzzle(); drawControls();
  movementEl.querySelector("svg")!.setAttribute("data-state", named);
}
(window as any).__bench = {
  states: () => Object.keys(STATES),
  describe: () => (named ? STATES[named].describe : "free-running"),
  check: () => {
    if (!named) return [];
    const e = STATES[named].expect;
    const out: { name: string; pass: boolean; detail: string }[] = [];
    const g = shapes(esc, pose);
    let worst = -Infinity;
    for (const tooth of g.teeth) for (const st of [g.entryStone, g.exitStone]) worst = Math.max(worst, stonePenetration(tooth, st));
    out.push({ name: "no tooth inside a stone", pass: worst <= CONTACT_TOL * 1.01, detail: `max penetration ${worst.toExponential(2)}` });
    out.push({ name: "lever within bankings", pass: Math.abs(pose.forkAngle) <= derived(esc).forkHalf + 1e-9, detail: `fork ${pose.forkAngle.toFixed(3)}°` });
    if (e.phase) out.push({ name: "escapement phase", pass: pose.phase === e.phase, detail: `got ${pose.phase}, expected ${e.phase}` });
    if (e.running !== undefined) out.push({ name: "running", pass: reading.running === e.running, detail: `running=${reading.running}` });
    if (e.rateWithin && tg) out.push({ name: "timegrapher rate", pass: tg.rateSecondsPerDay >= e.rateWithin[0] && tg.rateSecondsPerDay <= e.rateWithin[1], detail: `${tg.rateSecondsPerDay.toFixed(1)} s/day, expected ${e.rateWithin.join("..")}` });
    if (e.amplitudeWithin && tg) out.push({ name: "timegrapher amplitude", pass: tg.amplitudeDeg >= e.amplitudeWithin[0] && tg.amplitudeDeg <= e.amplitudeWithin[1], detail: `${tg.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(1)}°, expected ${e.amplitudeWithin.join("..")}` });
    if (e.beatErrorBelow !== undefined && tg) out.push({ name: "beat error", pass: tg.beatErrorMs < e.beatErrorBelow, detail: `${tg.beatErrorMs.toFixed(2)} ms` });
    out.push({ name: "instrument agrees with physics on rate", pass: !tg || !reading.running || Math.abs(tg.rateSecondsPerDay - reading.rateSecondsPerDay) < 0.5, detail: `instrument ${tg?.rateSecondsPerDay.toFixed(2)} vs true ${reading.rateSecondsPerDay.toFixed(2)}` });
    return out;
  },
};

if (!named) { loadPuzzle(PUZZLES[0].id); drawMovement(); drawTimegrapher(); }
requestAnimationFrame(frame);
EOF

Key findings for the sim: - Beat = one half-swing = one tick. beat period = 3600/bph, oscillation period T = 7200/bph, f = bph/7200. Verified against Ciechanowski and ETA CT 2824-2 (28'800 alt/h). - Rate: rate_s_per_day = (T_nominal / T_measured - 1) * 86400, + = fast. Verified from tg source (computer.c). - Amplitude: A = (lift/2) / sin(pi * dt / T), dt = unlock-to-lock interval, T = full oscillation period. Verified from tg source (algo.c), and it is the exact SHM solution. The formula in your brief (lift / (2pi*dt/T)) is only the small-angle approximation; use the sine form. At 52°, 28,800 bph, 280° gives dt = 7.4 ms. - Beat error: tg computes |T/2 - d1| = |d2 - d1| / 2, which equals the trace-line separation. Whether Witschi/Weishi show the half-difference or the full difference I could NOT verify from a manual. Flagged as medium confidence. - Lift angle: 52° is the machine default (tg DEFAULT_LA, Weishi manual via snippet, Caliber Corner). ETA's own document states 50° for the 2824-2. Watchguy table: 7750 49°, 6497 44°, Seiko 7S26 53°. - Trace: one dot per beat, position = tick offset mod beat period, slope proportional to rate, two lines separated by beat error. tg strip width = beat period/10. - Three sounds per beat (unlock, impulse, lock) and "first to third pulse spans the lift angle" come from a forum quote attributed to Witschi training material; marked secondary. The real Witschi training PDF was not found online. - Tolerances: ETA grade rate figures (±12/±7/±4 s/d) only from Wikipedia; ETA amplitude and beat-error limits not found. Research done: /Users/ahp/.personal/code/websites/anthropic/docs/research/03-amplitude-and-isochronism.md (about 75 lines, no other files touched).

Headline findings: 1. Sign of escapement error: the brief's premise ("gains at low amplitude because the impulse is mostly an advance") is NOT what the primary sources say. Airy 1826 (read directly), Hoyng arXiv:1501.03673 Eq. 10/30, an industry patent US 9,323,223 and SJX all agree: for the Swiss lever, unlocking (before line of centres) = loss, impulse before centre = gain, impulse after centre + run to banking = loss; net effect is a LOSS that grows as amplitude falls (~1/A). Real flat-spring watches nonetheless often gain as they run down, because the regulator-pin/hairspring interaction is set to over-compensate; the patent says designers aim for a hairspring gain of 2-8 s/d between 300° and 150° to cancel the escapement loss. Recommended sim model: r(A) = r0 - k_e(A_ref/A - 1) + k_p(A_ref - A)/10°, with k_e ≈ 8 s/d, k_p ≈ 0.8 s/d per 10° (net ≈ +1 s/d per 10° drop, matching Witschi's worked example); k_p = 0 for overcoil/no-pin calibres, k_p = 5-8 for the "spring resting on a pin" fault. 2. Amplitude: Witschi says 270-310° full wind, lift angle ~51°. Healthy watch drops ~10-15% in 24 h (280° -> ~250°). The brief's 280° -> 200° is a tired-spring/dirty-train state: fine for the afternoon-slump puzzle, not the healthy default. 3. Torque curve: ~flat middle, <=15% torque drop at the escape wheel in the first day (WatchTime rule of thumb), steep fall in the last turns; ~6 turns x 7.5 h per turn. Amplitude ∝ torque^k with k between 0.5 (viscous losses ∝ A², Hoyng) and 1 (Coulomb); recommended k = 0.7. No measured N·mm-vs-hours dataset for a named calibre found. 4. Knocking: above ~320-330° the impulse pin hits the back of the fork horn, truncating the swing -> sudden large gain (Horopedia: "exaggerated advance"); timegrapher amplitude becomes meaningless. 5. Could not verify: Daniels/de Carle text (not online), Minnix 1968 lever model (DTIC under maintenance), a universal s/day-per-degree coefficient (none exists in the sources). Ciechanowski has no amplitude/isochronism numbers.

Assistant2026-11-03T16:52:15.063Z

Verdict: workable, and already past the riskiest part. The brief's own gate was "can the escapement be made to lock, impulse and drop correctly in 2D?" It can, the invariants are tested, and you confirmed it by eye at 1/20 speed. Everything after that was physics plumbing, and the physics held up better than the brief expected.

What the spike found

  • The escapement works as a pure kinematic stepper with exact geometry. Seven correction rounds, which fails the brief's soft "three or fewer" line, but none reintroduced an earlier bug. Two rounds were wasted diagnoses.
  • The hard part was not drawing but geometry: pallet faces must be arcs about the fork pivot, and the let-off corner has to be placed by construction. Both are real escapement-design facts, not simulation hacks.
  • Every angle I guessed for the spike checks out against Playtner (1910). The drawing is technically an English tooth form on a Swiss layout, with zero draw. Nobody but a watchmaker will notice, and the glossary says so.

What the research found

  • The period, regulator and inertia formulas are solid and reproduce a published worked example to within 10%.
  • The timegrapher math is verified line by line against an open-source timegrapher. The brief's amplitude formula was the small-angle approximation; the exact one is in the code.
  • The brief's isochronism premise was backwards, and so was mine when I briefed the agent. The escapement alone makes a lever watch lose at low amplitude. The gain real watches show comes from the regulator pins over-compensating. The model has both terms, and puzzle 3's text now teaches the correct version.
  • The brief's "280° to 200° after a day" describes a tired mainspring, not a healthy watch. Healthy is roughly 280° to 250°. That made puzzle 3 better, since the fault is now a real fault.
  • Poise error has a closed-form model with a Bessel function, from a Rolex patent. The famous 220° rule is just the first zero of that function.
  • Three claims stay medium confidence: regulator sensitivity per degree, the vertical amplitude drop, and the split between the two isochronism terms. None affects whether the puzzles teach the right lesson.

Where it stands

  • Core built: 46 tests, four puzzles loading, puzzle 1 proven solvable end to end, eight render states passing numeric and visual checks.
  • Not done: deploy (hosting agent), design polish, and the cold-reviewer test of puzzle 1 that only you can run.

My concerns, in order

  1. Readability for a non-expert. The trace and readouts are faithful to a real timegrapher, which is the pitch, but a reviewer with no watch knowledge sees a sloping green line and a number. Puzzle 1's symptom text does the explaining. Whether that lands in 30 seconds is the one thing I can't measure.
  2. Puzzle 4 has no fix. Poising isn't a control, so it is diagnose-only. Honest, but a reviewer may read it as unfinished. Either add a "move weight to position X" control as the first stretch item or hide the puzzle.
  3. Design is functional, not distinctive. Paper background, monospace, a green timegrapher screen. It reads as a tool, which fits, but it will not stand out next to Ciechanowski's work. A polish pass is worth an hour, no more.
  4. Time. You are well inside the 8-hour limit on build work, but the deploy, the video and the design doc are still ahead, and the judgment log plus SPIKE.md are raw material rather than a finished doc.

Recommendation: ship it. Deploy the core as is, spend one hour on design polish and puzzle 4's control, then stop adding and write the doc. The transcripts already contain what the brief asked to see: a spike that nearly failed its round count, tests restated for stated reasons, and two horology claims corrected by sources before they became code.

  it("removing weight on the wrong side doubles the error, 90° off leaves it at √2", () => {

    expect(readWatch(w, { ...base, poiseCorrectionDeg: 180 }).netUnbalance).toBeCloseTo(20e-11, 20);
    expect(readWatch(w, { ...base, poiseCorrectionDeg: 90 }).netUnbalance).toBeCloseTo(Math.SQRT2 * 10e-11, 20);
  });
});
